candidate.title: Redis throttle key is set before retrieval succeeds, suppressing retries after failures
reports: $redis.setnx lock in topicretriever.rb is not released or handled if performretrieve raises, causing legitimate retries within 60s to be silently dropped after a failed fetch

[bug] the 60-second throttle key is written to redis (setnx + expire) inside retrievedrecently? before performretrieve runs, so the key is committed before the retrieval operation has succeeded. when performretrieve raises (network error, 404, readability failure), the key persists for 60 seconds so every subsequent retry job executes retrieve, hits retrievedrecently? and returns silently — retries no-op 'successfully' while no topic is created, and the failure is never surfaced to anyone.

[bug] the throttle key is committed via $redis.setnx before performretrieve runs, so a failed or failed-early retrieval still marks the embedurl as 'retrieved' and blocks all retries for 60 seconds if importremote raises or the user lookup returns nil on the first attempt, subsequent embed page loads within 60s skip retrieval entirely; the throttle key expires but each retry re-arms it, so a persistently failing url is retried at most once per 60s per visitor with no error recorded anywhere

[bug] the 'retrieved recently' redis marker is committed (setnx + expire) before performretrieve runs, so a failed retrieval leaves the marker in place for its full 60-second ttl. every retry within the next 60 seconds — retries of the failed job and the loading page's 30-second re-enqueues — enters retrieve, sees the marker, and returns success without attempting the work, so the system reports success while the retrieval never happened; recovery depends entirely on the user keeping the page open past the throttle window.

duplicate_of.reason: Both findings describe the same core bug: the Redis throttle/lock key is written before a successful retrieval, so failures (exceptions) cause subsequent Sidekiq retries within the TTL to be suppressed, though Finding A additionally notes the non-atomic setnx+expire as an extra edge-case risk.
